source.title: A Bayesian Perspective on Generalization and Stochastic Gradient Descent
source.authors: Samuel L. Smith; Quoc V. Le

record.file_problem: none; full conference paper text supplied
record.tranche_reason: Tests the coexistence of fitting random labels and generalizing on natural labels in logistic regression, and tests batch-size effects on test accuracy with a shallow network. These are related measurements and settings rather than the original deep-network studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own logistic-regression results on random and informative MNIST labels, and its own batch-size, learning-rate, training-set-size, momentum, and L2-regularization experiments. Cited findings from Zhang et al., Keskar et al., and others are not rows. Figure-only values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study directly tests V1's coexistence phenomenon in a new setting: the same binary logistic-regression model generalizes on informative labels and memorizes randomized labels. Its batch-size experiments hold gradient updates fixed, rather than epochs, so they do not establish V5's fixed-epoch comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors report coexistence of informative-label generalization and random-label memorization in logistic regression, interpret it through Bayesian evidence, and empirically verify scaling relations between optimal batch size, learning rate, training-set size, and momentum. The explanation that mini-batch noise favors high-evidence minima is a proposed mechanism, rather than a directly measured causal result.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses binary logistic regression for the random-label/generalization experiment and a shallow 800-unit ReLU MNIST network for batch-size experiments; the source methods and larger benchmark settings in the claim versions are not reproduced.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch-size outcomes vary with learning rate, training-set size, momentum, and L2 regularization.

fits_no_version.finding: Informative-label predictions can be accurate but overconfident; Bayesian evidence and test cross-entropy vary together across regularization strengths. This is not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness versus training–test accuracy gap comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this binary logistic-regression experiment, Bayesian evidence tracks test cross-entropy across regularization strengths.

fits_no_version.finding: Under fixed update budgets, shallow-network test accuracy peaks at an intermediate batch size. The peak shifts with learning rate, dataset size, and momentum; L2 regularization shrinks the batch-size accuracy difference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch-size effects under fixed gradient-update budgets depend on optimization hyperparameters, dataset size, and regularization.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors explicitly report being unable to observe a batch-size generalization gap in linear models, without providing a fixed-epoch protocol or numerical comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The batch-size accuracy gap observed in the shallow nonlinear network was not observed in the authors' linear-model experiments.

record.problems: The experiments use a small binary MNIST logistic-regression task and a shallow network trained on only 1000 MNIST images, rather than the named large-scale settings. Most results are given qualitatively in text or figures without exact test-accuracy values. The authors note that the batch-gradient Gaussian approximation may be imperfect, especially for sparse, heavy-tailed gradients.

untested.parts: The named deep architectures, multiclass datasets, ImageNet's incomplete random-label fit, and the specified absence of explicit regularization are not reproduced.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No explicitly matched fixed-epoch batch-size comparison, including a controlled demonstration that adapting the recipe removes a penalty within that budget.
No magnitude-scaled perturbation measure, training–test gap ranking, or comparison against norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal and retraining experiment based on example memorization.

missing.what: Informative-label training cross-entropy falls to zero under weak regularization. This supplies the natural-label training-fit component of the coexistence comparison, which R1 records only through test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source listed for any version. Qualitative accuracy statements suffice for the V1 verdict; exact figure values are unavailable in the supplied text. States marked cannot_determine for unlinked rows concern their ability to establish a claim version, not whether their reported findings occurred.

versions.untested_parts: Tests a 784-weight logistic regression on a balanced binary MNIST subset, not the specified Inception, AlexNet, MLP, or ImageNet networks; does not report numerical accuracy values in text.

Uses a shallow MNIST network with 1000 training images and reports test-accuracy changes by batch size; does not test the cited image-classification/language benchmark conditions or compare workload-dependent large-batch thresholds. It also reports a separate L2 regularization condition.

rows.subject: logistic regression
rows.operation_detail: Trained on informative labels matching true MNIST labels, with regularization varied; the text describes weak regularization qualitatively.

conditions.value: balanced MNIST subset; 800 training images, half labels “0” and half “1”; test set of 5000 zeros and 5000 ones

rows.value: generalizes well on the test set
rows.note: The paper states the qualitative outcome; no numerical accuracy is given in the text.
rows.check: The qualitative accuracy result is correctly recorded. This extends the coexistence phenomenon to weakly regularized binary logistic regression; it does not reproduce the named neural-network experiments.

rows.subject: logistic regression
rows.operation_detail: Trained on randomized labels of the same inputs, with regularization varied; the text describes weak regularization qualitatively.

conditions.value: same balanced MNIST inputs and train/test split as the informative-label experiment

rows.measure: training-set fit and test-set prediction performance
rows.value: perfectly memorizes the random labels; test cross-entropy explodes and predictions are random
rows.note: The result supports fitting arbitrary training labels while the corresponding random-label test performance fails to generalize. Text does not give test accuracy numerically.
rows.check: Correct qualitative result. Both training and test labels were randomized; the model perfectly memorizes training labels and makes random test predictions. Binary chance accuracy is 50%, although no numerical test accuracy is supplied.

rows.subject: logistic regression
rows.operation_detail: Trained on informative labels matching true MNIST labels, with regularization varied.

conditions.value: balanced MNIST subset; 800 training images, half labels “0” and half “1”; test set of 5000 zeros and 5000 ones

rows.baseline: ln 2 is the equal-probability reference stated in the text
rows.value: high while weakly regularized; predictions are accurate but overconfident
rows.note: This cross-entropy outcome shows overconfidence despite accurate classification; it is not an accuracy value.
rows.check: High test cross-entropy measures overconfidence, whereas V1 specifies held-out accuracy. Accurate but overconfident predictions do not make the accuracy-based coexistence effect partial.

rows.subject: shallow neural network with 800 hidden units and RELU hidden activations
rows.operation_detail: Trained with full batches of 1000 images at constant learning rate 1.0 and momentum 0.9, without regularization.
rows.baseline: small batches of 30 images show a clear accuracy advantage after a thousand gradient updates
rows.value: lower test accuracy than small-batch training; a peak across batch sizes is reported
rows.note: The text describes the comparison and peak without numerical accuracy values.
rows.check: The lower full-batch accuracy is reported, but comparisons use gradient updates rather than equal epochs. At 10000 updates, B=1000 processes approximately 10000 epochs and B=30 approximately 300 epochs. Figure 3 supplies trajectories; Figure 4 supplies the 10000-step endpoint.

rows.subject: shallow neural network with 800 hidden units and RELU hidden activations
rows.operation_detail: Swept batch sizes from 1 to 1000 at constant learning rate 1.0 and momentum 0.9, without regularization; evaluated after 10000 steps.
rows.value: a clear peak emerges; an optimum batch size maximizes test accuracy; model cannot train when batch size B / 10
rows.note: Batch sizes and the peak are described in the text; no peak value is supplied.
rows.check: The accuracy peak is real, but fixed updates give different epoch budgets across batch sizes. The expression 'B / 10' is corrupted mathematical text describing failure at very small batches, not a readable numerical condition.

rows.subject: shallow neural network with 800 hidden units and RELU hidden activations
rows.operation_detail: Compared small-batch and full-batch training with L2 regularization coefficient λ = 0.1.
rows.measure: generalization gap in test accuracy; test cross-entropy
rows.value: regularization significantly reduced the size of the generalization gap; regularized full-batch training achieved slightly lower test accuracy than unregularized small-batch training and also lower test cross-entropy
rows.note: The paper explicitly says the gap is reduced, not eliminated. It also reports that regularized-model test cross-entropy does not degrade after many gradient updates.
rows.check: L2 regularization reduces the batch-size accuracy gap, but no fixed-epoch comparison is established. The row also combines accuracy and cross-entropy, and compares both regularized batch sizes with an unregularized small-batch baseline; these are distinct comparisons.

rows.subject: shallow neural network with 800 hidden units and RELU hidden activations
rows.operation_detail: Varied learning rate and batch size while measuring test accuracy after (10000/ε) steps.
rows.measure: test-set accuracy as a function of batch size
rows.value: the performance peak shifts right as ε increases; peak accuracy begins to fall once ε ∼ 3 and falls rapidly above this point
rows.uncertainty: error bars are distance from best observed batch size to the next batch size sampled
rows.note: The text reports that the peak's location and achievable accuracy depend on learning rate.
rows.check: The learning-rate sweep uses 10000/epsilon updates, with epoch exposure also depending on batch size. It demonstrates scaling of the optimal batch size and a high-learning-rate accuracy penalty, but does not explicitly report V5's fixed-epoch comparison.

rows.subject: shallow neural network with 800 hidden units and RELU hidden activations
rows.operation_detail: Varied training-set size and batch size at ε = 1; evaluated after 10000 steps and averaged curves over five experiments.

conditions.value: range; curves averaged over five experiments

rows.measure: test-set accuracy as a function of batch size
rows.value: peak shifts right as training-set size rises; overall model performance improves; generalization gap becomes less pronounced as training-set size increases
rows.uncertainty: curves averaged over five experiments; no other uncertainty stated
rows.note: This varies training-set size, which qualifies the batch-size effect.
rows.check: Training-set and batch sizes vary while updates remain fixed, so epoch budgets vary. The result cannot establish V5. The text further qualifies proportional scaling of optimal batch size with dataset size as appearing once N is roughly above 20000.

rows.subject: shallow neural network with 800 hidden units and RELU hidden activations
rows.operation_detail: Varied momentum coefficient and batch size at ε = 1; evaluated after 10000 gradient updates.
rows.measure: test-set performance as a function of batch size
rows.value: peak moves right as momentum coefficient increases; best observed batch size agrees remarkably well with the proposed scaling rule
rows.note: The reported behavior concerns the location of the accuracy peak, rather than a direct fixed-epoch comparison of large and small batches.
rows.check: The momentum-dependent shift in optimal batch size is reported after fixed gradient updates, not equal epochs. Agreement with the proposed scaling rule does not itself measure V5's fixed-epoch penalty.

relationships.condition: Weakly regularized binary logistic regression on the same 800 MNIST inputs with informative versus randomized labels
relationships.reason: R1 reports good informative-label test accuracy; R2 reports perfect random-label memorization and random test predictions, extending the coexistence phenomenon to a linear model.
relationships.display_finding: The reported informative-label generalization, perfect random-label memorization and random test predictions remain unverified from the available source.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
